label: Reply to appointment emails with free Google Calendar slots via AI
description: When I get a new email, analyze the mail for the patient name, the type of appointment and doctor and the date-time. Get all free time slots that are at least 45 minutes long. Finally, send an email with all the available appointments.

triggers.label: Poll all new emails
triggers.description: Polls Gmail and starts a run for each new email. Only the message ID is used, to fetch the full email in the next step.
triggers.name: trigger_1

tasks.label: Get an email from the trigger
tasks.description: Fetches the full email from the trigger by its ID, including the plain-text body and the sender, CC and BCC addresses used for the reply.
tasks.name: googleMail_1

tasks.label: Convert the mail into a json
tasks.description: Reads the email body and returns JSON: whether it is an appointment request, the patient's name, the type of doctor, and the requested date-time window (start and end).
tasks.name: openAi_1

messages.content:

tasks.description: Continues only if OpenAI marked the email as an appointment request. Any other email is logged and skipped, so it gets no reply.

caseTrue.label: Get free time slots
caseTrue.description: Looks up the free time slots in your calendar between the start and end of the requested window. Select the calendar to check.
caseTrue.name: googleCalendar_1

caseTrue.label: Loop through dates
caseTrue.description: Goes through each free time slot returned by Google Calendar and keeps the ones long enough for an appointment.
caseTrue.name: loop_1

iteratee.label: If a time slot is longer than 45 minutes
iteratee.description: Checks whether the current slot is longer than 45 minutes, the length of one appointment.
iteratee.name: condition_1

caseTrue.label: Append to a list
caseTrue.description: Slot is long enough: appends it to the validTimeSlots list kept for this run.
caseTrue.name: dataStorage_1

caseFalse.label: Log Warning
caseFalse.description: Slot is too short: logs a warning with the slot, so you can see which slots were skipped.
caseFalse.name: logEntryWarn1

caseTrue.label: Get stored list
caseTrue.description: Reads the validTimeSlots list built by the loop. If no slot qualified, it returns the default value, so replace that example slot with something sensible or remove it.

Each appointment lasts 45 minutes and can start at every quarter of an hour at 00, 15, 30, and 45. Appointments cannot overlap. Provide a response in the format "1. date of appointment start time - end time" and so on. Do not include any additional explanation.

stickyNotes.content:
## Setup: calendar and a test email

1. Add your Gmail connection to the trigger and both Gmail steps, and your OpenAI connection to both OpenAI steps.
2. Select the calendar to offer times from in **Get free time slots**.
3. Send the inbox a test request, such as *I'd like to book a dermatology appointment for Jane Doe next Tuesday between 9:00 and 12:00*, then click **Test**.
4. When no free slot is long enough, **Get stored list** falls back to an example slot from 2024. Replace it with a value that suits your calendar, or clear it.

## Watch out: replies go to real senders

OpenAI decides whether each new email is an appointment request. Every email it marks as one gets an automatic reply with suggested times.

Try it on a separate inbox first, and check the **Log skipped email** entries to see what was left alone. The workflow only suggests times; it doesn't book anything in the calendar.
